words: count; number; ones; tens; one hundred
notes: Say the counting words to 100 by ones and by tens, as a daily routine that grows all year (to 10, to 20, then by tens to 100, then by ones to 100). Students who can say the sequence fluently have attention left for pairing words with objects (Progressions, PDF 16 (printed 10)); counting by tens starts the decade-word pattern grade 1 needs (Progressions, PDF 61 (printed 55)). Oral only: reading and writing numerals stops at 20 in K (K.CC.A.3). Limit: to 100. Cluster K.CC.A, major. IM Kindergarten units 1, 2, 4 to 8 carry it as warm-ups and the counting centers; it closes in unit 8.

words: count on; start at; next
notes: Start the count from any number within the known sequence (start at 6 and count to 11) instead of from 1. This is the prerequisite for grade 1 counting on (Progressions, PDF 17 (printed 11)). Numbers within the sequence the child knows, mostly within 20, later to 100 in jumps from decades. No adding yet: the count starts from a spoken number, not from a group. Cluster K.CC.A, major. IM Kindergarten units 4 to 6 and 8 (counting routines in later units).

words: count; touch; one each
notes: Count objects by pairing each word with one and only one object, using a pointing or moving act to keep word and object together (Progressions, PDF 16 (printed 10)). Small collections first (to 5, then 10), objects in a line before scattered ones. Typical error: skipping or double-counting an object, saying words faster than touches. Feeds mk-how-many in the same grade. Cluster K.CC.B, major. IM Kindergarten unit 1 (Math in Our World, sections B and D, counting collections).

words: how many; last number; same; zero
notes: Owns the parent K.CC.B.4 (connect counting to cardinality; its parts a and c sit in mk-one-to-one and mk-one-more). The last number said tells how many, and the count does not change when the objects are moved or counted in another order (Progressions, PDF 17 (printed 11)). Count to answer how many and count out a given number, within 10 in this row: objects in a line, an array or a circle, and scattered sets; write the numerals 0 to 10 (0 for an empty set). Introduces the 5-frame and the 10-frame (ten-frame) as a structured place for 10 objects. Starts K.CC.B.5 and K.CC.A.3, which mk-count-to-20 completes to 20. Typical error: answering how many by recounting from 1 or by repeating the whole count. Cluster K.CC.B (and K.CC.A), major. IM Kindergarten unit 2 (Numbers 1 to 10), sections A to C.

words: one more; next number
notes: Each next counting word means one more object: add one object to a counted group of 6 and say 7 without recounting (Progressions, PDF 17 (printed 11), "the conceptual start for Grade 1 counting on"). Within 10, then within 20 in unit 6. Uses the ten-frame to see one more fill the next box. Cluster K.CC.B, major. IM Kindergarten unit 2 lessons 16 to 18, revisited in units 4, 6 and 8.

words: more; fewer; less; same; match
notes: Say whether one group has more than, fewer than or the same number as another, first by matching objects one to one and seeing extras, then by counting both and using the count sequence (the number later in the sequence is greater) (Progressions, PDF 17 to 18 (printed 11 to 12)). Groups up to 10. Key misconception: the group that is spread out or looks bigger has more. Only which is more, not how many more (that is grade 1). Cluster K.CC.C, major. IM Kindergarten unit 1 section C (Are There Enough?) and unit 2 sections A and B.

words: greater; less; equal; number
notes: Compare two numbers from 1 to 10 given as written numerals, by thinking of the counts or the count sequence. Words only: the symbols greater than, less than and equal are grade 1 (1.NBT.B.3). Limit: numerals 1 to 10. Cluster K.CC.C, major. IM Kindergarten unit 2 section D (Compare Numbers), lessons 17 to 22.

words: eleven to twenty; teen number; count out; numeral
notes: Completes K.CC.B.5 and K.CC.A.3 from mk-how-many: count to tell how many with up to 20 objects in a line, an array or a circle, or up to 10 scattered; count out a given number from 1 to 20; write numerals 0 to 20 and match them to collections. Limits are the standard's own (20 arranged, 10 scattered); counting a circle needs a start mark, an array needs row-by-row tracking (Progressions, PDF 16 (printed 10)). Two ten-frames show teen collections. Cluster K.CC.B and K.CC.A, major. IM Kindergarten unit 6 (Numbers 0 to 20), sections A and C.

words: put together; add; take away; take from; in all; left
notes: Addition as putting together or adding to, subtraction as taking apart or taking from, shown with objects, fingers, drawings, sounds and acting out, within 10. Students count all (Level 1 methods) and say what they did. No symbols yet in this row: mk-add-sub-expressions records with + and - and owns K.OA.A.1. Cluster K.OA.A, major. IM Kindergarten unit 4 section A (Count to Add and Subtract).

words: story problem; how many in all; how many are left; add; subtract
cross_subject: ela:SL.K.2 (story problems are heard read aloud and retold before solving)
notes: Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 10 with objects or drawings: Add To and Take From with the result unknown, Put Together/Take Apart with total unknown and with both addends unknown; the easiest Take Apart with addend unknown may be acted out but full competence with it is grade 1 (Progressions, PDF 25 to 26 (printed 19 to 20)). Compare problems are not K. Students tell the story back and show it. Limit: totals within 10. Cluster K.OA.A, major. IM Kindergarten unit 4 section B and unit 5 section B (More Types of Story Problems).

words: plus; minus; equals; expression; equation
notes: Owns K.OA.A.1 (started in mk-add-sub-meaning): write and read addition and subtraction expressions and simple equations within 10 (3 + 2, 5 - 1, 5 = 3 + 2) and match them to objects, drawings and stories. Equations with the total on the left are used on purpose so the equal sign is not read only as "the answer comes next" (Progressions, PDF 25 (printed 19), MP.6). Limit: within 10; symbols for the unknown are grade 1. Cluster K.OA.A, major. IM Kindergarten unit 4 section C (Addition and Subtraction Expressions).

words: partners; break apart; make; equation
notes: Decompose each number up to 10 into pairs in more than one way (7 is 5 and 2, 4 and 3, 6 and 1) with objects, fingers, 5-frames and 10-frames, shake-and-spill counters and drawings; record each pair with a drawing or an equation such as 7 = 4 + 3. The 5-and-some pattern is used on purpose (Progressions, PDF 25 to 26 (printed 19 to 20)). Zero cases may be shown once and then left out of practice. Limit: numbers to 10. This is prerequisite b for grade 1 make-ten (Progressions, PDF 31 (printed 25)). Cluster K.OA.A, major. IM Kindergarten unit 5 sections A and C.

words: make ten; partner; how many more
notes: For any number from 1 to 9 find the number that makes 10 (7 and 3), on a 10-frame and with fingers, and record it with a drawing or equation (7 + 3 = 10). Prerequisite a for grade 1 make-ten methods (Progressions, PDF 31 (printed 25)). Limit: partners of 10 only. Cluster K.OA.A, major. IM Kindergarten unit 5 section C (Make and Break Apart 10), unit 8 section D (All About 10).

words: add; subtract; just know
notes: Add and subtract within 5 accurately and quickly, from decompositions of 5 and earlier Add To and Take From work (Progressions, PDF 26 (printed 20)); equations such as 2 + 1 = ? and 3 - 1 = ? still tied to a story or a picture. Practised in short spaced games and centers (shake and spill, behind my back), never with a timer shown to the student. Limit: within 5. Cluster K.OA.A, major. IM Kindergarten unit 5 and unit 8 section C (Fluency within 5).

words: ten ones; and some more; teen number
notes: Compose and decompose 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones (18 = 10 + 8) with two ten-frames, towers of 10 cubes and drawings, recording with an equation. The ten is still ten ones, not yet a unit called a ten (that is grade 1). English teen words hide the structure ("fourteen" says the 4 first), so say both forms (Progressions, PDF 61 (printed 55)). Prerequisite c for grade 1 make-ten (Progressions, PDF 31 (printed 25)). Limit: 11 to 19. Cluster K.NBT.A, major. IM Kindergarten unit 6 section B (10 Ones and Some More).

words: sort; group; category; most; fewest
cross_subject: science:K-ESS2-1 (count sunny, cloudy and rainy days and sort the counts); ela:L.K.5a (sort common objects into categories)
notes: Classify objects into given categories, count each category and order the categories by count. Limit from the Progressions table: each category count 10 or less (PDF 80 (printed 74)). Sorting rules come from the teacher first, later from students; the same objects can be sorted different ways (PDF 81 (printed 75)). Practises counting and comparing (K.CC), which is why it is a supporting cluster: K.MD.B, supporting. No graphs required. Teacher note: sort objects and pictures, not classmates by body, family or home features. IM Kindergarten unit 1 section A, units 3, 7 and 8.

words: longer; shorter; taller; heavier; lighter; holds more
cross_subject: science:K-PS2-1 (compare which push made the ball go farther)
notes: Name measurable attributes of one object (length, weight, how much it holds) instead of the undifferentiated "bigger", and compare two objects directly by lining up endpoints, hefting or pouring, saying which has more of the attribute. Endpoints must be aligned; children may not conserve length when a stick is turned or a string is bent (Progressions, PDF 96 (printed 90)). No units or numbers yet. Cluster K.MD.A, additional. IM Kindergarten unit 3 lessons 6 to 7 and unit 7 section B (lessons 8 to 9).

words: circle; triangle; square; rectangle; hexagon; above; below; beside; in front of; behind; next to
cross_subject: social-studies:ssk-position-words (the same position words are used to describe places)
notes: Name flat shapes (circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon) in the environment and correctly whatever their size or orientation, including non-prototypes (a "skinny" triangle, a tilted square), and describe where objects are with above, below, beside, in front of, behind, next to (Progressions, PDF 123 (printed 117)). Typical error: a square turned on its corner called a diamond and not a square. Cluster K.G.A, additional. IM Kindergarten unit 3 section A (Exploring Shapes in Our Environment).

words: flat; solid; side; corner; cube; sphere; cylinder; cone
cross_subject: ela:L.K.5a (sort objects such as shapes into categories)
notes: Tell flat (two-dimensional) shapes from solid (three-dimensional) ones, and compare shapes of different sizes and orientations in informal words: number of sides and corners, sides of equal length, faces of a solid that are flat shapes (Progressions, PDF 123 to 124 (printed 117 to 118)). Solids named: cube, sphere, cylinder, cone. Definitions are not expected; describing and explaining a sort is. Clusters K.G.A (additional) and K.G.B (supporting: it practises counting sides and comparing). IM Kindergarten unit 3 lessons 1 to 9 (flat) and unit 7 section B (Describe, Compare, and Create Solid Shapes).

words: build; put together; make a shape
notes: Build shapes from parts (sticks and clay balls), draw shapes, and compose simple shapes into larger ones (two triangles with full sides touching make a rectangle), first by trial and error, then by attributes (Progressions, PDF 120 (printed 114)). Pattern blocks and outline puzzles; count the pieces used (K.CC). Cluster K.G.B, supporting. IM Kindergarten unit 3 section B (Making Shapes) and unit 7 section A (Compose and Count with Flat Shapes).

words: count on; count back; start at; jumps
notes: Relate counting to adding and subtracting: count on 2 from 6 to add 2, count on from 9 to 13 to find 13 - 9 as an unknown addend. Counting on is a thinking strategy (the first addend is embedded in the total), not a rote trick; counting on to subtract is easier than counting down and keeps subtraction tied to addition (Progressions, PDF 29 to 30 (printed 23 to 24)). Fingers or head bobs track the count. Within 20. No number line (Progressions, PDF 32 (printed 26)). Cluster 1.OA.C, major. IM Grade 1 unit 1 section A and unit 3.

words: sum; difference; just know; double
notes: Begins 1.OA.C.6 (owned by m1-add-sub-within-20): fluency for addition and subtraction within 10, from decompositions, doubles, plus 0 and plus 1 patterns and the related addition for a subtraction. Fluent means accurate and reasonably fast, a mix of just knowing, patterns and strategies (Progressions, PDF 33 (printed 27)). Short spaced practice, no timer shown. Cluster 1.OA.C, major. IM Grade 1 unit 1 section A and unit 3 section A (Develop Fluency with Addition and Subtraction within 10).

words: make a ten; ten and some more; doubles; related fact
notes: Add and subtract within 20 with Level 2 and 3 strategies: counting on, making ten (8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 14), decomposing to a ten (13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1), the related addition (8 + 4 = 12 so 12 - 8 = 4) and known sums (6 + 7 = 6 + 6 + 1). Make-ten rests on three K pieces: partners of 10, all decompositions below 10, teens as 10 + ones (Progressions, PDF 31 (printed 25)). Two ten-frames show the strategy and are tied to the written equations. Fluency is required only within 10 here; within 20 is grade 2 (2.OA.B.2). Cluster 1.OA.C, major. IM Grade 1 unit 3 sections B to D, unit 8 section A.

words: turn around; any order; group; make a ten
notes: Use the commutative property (8 + 3 = 3 + 8, count on from the larger addend) and the associative property (2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10) as strategies. Students apply them; the property names are not required of students. Whole numbers within 20. Subtraction is not commutative; check it with a story. Cluster 1.OA.B, major. IM Grade 1 unit 2 lessons 6 to 9 and unit 3 (three-addend and make-ten work).

words: add to; take from; result; change; how many now
cross_subject: ela:SL.1.2 (retell key details of a story problem read aloud)
notes: Add To and Take From story problems within 20 with the result or the change unknown, shown with objects, drawings and a situation equation with a symbol for the unknown (5 + ? = 8). Start-unknown problems are met here but are among the hardest subtypes (Progressions, PDF 29 (printed 23)). Begins 1.OA.A.1, owned by m1-all-problem-types. Cluster 1.OA.A, major. IM Grade 1 unit 2 section A.

words: put together; take apart; part; total; unknown addend
notes: Put Together/Take Apart problems with total, one addend or both addends unknown, within 20, and subtraction understood as an unknown-addend problem: find 10 - 8 by finding what makes 10 with 8. This meaning of subtraction is one students will need for negative numbers in the middle grades (Progressions, PDF 28 (printed 22)). Objects, drawings, equations. Owns 1.OA.B.4; contributes to 1.OA.A.1. Cluster 1.OA.A and 1.OA.B, major. IM Grade 1 unit 2 section B.

words: how many more; how many fewer; compare; difference
notes: Compare problems within 20 ("Julie has 3 more apples than Lucy"): the difference is not present in the situation and must be built in a drawing, by matching and finding the extra. The language is the hard part: students hear who has more but not how many more, and some read "less" as "more"; say the two parts as two sentences first (Progressions, PDF 27 (printed 21)). Matching drawings with labelled rows. Contributes to 1.OA.A.1. Cluster 1.OA.A, major. IM Grade 1 unit 2 section C.

words: story problem; unknown; equation; tape diagram
cross_subject: ela:RI.1.1 (ask and answer questions about key details in a short text)
notes: Owns 1.OA.A.1: all twelve problem subtypes, with unknowns in all positions, within 20, using objects, drawings and situation equations, then solution equations (14 - ? = 8 rewritten as 8 + ? = 14) (Progressions, PDF 28 (printed 22)). Introduces the tape diagram late in the year for Compare and part-whole problems, drawn from the matching drawings (Progressions, PDF 27 and 31 (printed 21 and 25)). Grade 1 students solve and discuss start-unknown and opposite-language Compare problems, but proficiency on those subtypes is a grade 2 target (Progressions, PDF 29 (printed 23)). Cluster 1.OA.A, major. IM Grade 1 unit 2 section D, unit 6 section C (All Kinds of Story Problems) and unit 8 section B.

words: three numbers; in all; add
notes: Word problems that add three whole numbers with a sum of 20 or less, with objects, drawings and an equation with a symbol for the unknown; choosing which two to add first (make a ten) links to m1-properties-strategies. Three-category data questions are one context (Progressions, PDF 82 (printed 76)). Limit: sum within 20. Cluster 1.OA.A, major. IM Grade 1 unit 2 lesson 21, unit 3 lessons 15 to 28, unit 8.

words: equal sign; the same as; true; false
notes: The equal sign means "the same as", not "the answer comes next": decide whether equations are true or false (6 = 6, 7 = 8 - 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2), with expressions on either side or both. Builds on K equations written with the total on the left (Progressions, PDF 25 (printed 19)). Within 20. Misconception named in advance: 4 + 1 = 5 + 2 judged true because 4 + 1 = 5. Cluster 1.OA.D, major. IM Grade 1 unit 2 lessons 2 to 17 and unit 3.

words: unknown; missing number; equation
notes: Find the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers, in any position: 8 + ? = 11, 5 = ? - 3, 6 + 6 = ?. Knowing where the total sits (alone on one side of an addition equation, first in a subtraction equation) lets students rewrite to a solution equation (Progressions, PDF 28 to 29 (printed 22 to 23)). Within 20. Cluster 1.OA.D, major. IM Grade 1 units 2 and 3 (lessons through unit 3 lesson 24), unit 4.

words: one hundred twenty; count; numeral; decade
notes: Count to 120 starting at any number below 120, and read and write numerals and match a numeral to a collection in that range. Hard spots: crossing a decade ("twenty-nine, twenty-ten") and crossing 100 (writing 1001 for 101) (Progressions, PDF 62 (printed 56)). Large collections are counted by grouping into tens. Limit: 120. Cluster 1.NBT.A, major. IM Grade 1 unit 4, unit 6 section B (measuring up to 120 units) and unit 8 section C (Numbers to 120).

words: ten; ones; bundle; teen number
notes: Ten ones can be thought of as one unit called a ten, and 11 to 19 are one ten and some ones (Progressions, PDF 62 (printed 56)). Introduces base-ten-blocks: towers of 10 connecting cubes and quick drawings where a ten is drawn as one stick, tied to the numeral (the 1 in 14 is 1 ten). A full ten-frame is the bridge from K. Limit: the unit ten only, two-digit numbers in m1-two-digit-place-value. Cluster 1.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 1 unit 3 section B (Add and Subtract using Ten as a Unit) and unit 4 section A (Units of Ten).

words: tens; ones; digit; two-digit number; tens place; ones place
notes: The two digits of a two-digit number are amounts of tens and ones (67 is 6 tens 7 ones; say it both ways), and 10, 20, ... 90 are one to nine tens and 0 ones. Decade words ("forty") must be learned as tens and are easily confused with teen words ("fourteen") (Progressions, PDF 62 (printed 56)). Base-ten blocks and drawings, layered place-value cards; different ways to make a number (4 tens 13 ones is 53). Limit: to 99. Cluster 1.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 1 unit 4 sections B and D.

words: greater than; less than; equal to; compare
notes: Compare two two-digit numbers by their tens and ones (the tens digit decides unless the tens are equal) and record with >, = and <. Teach the symbols from the math ("the wide side faces the larger number"), not with animal stories (Progressions, PDF 62 (printed 56)). Limit: two-digit numbers. Cluster 1.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 1 unit 4 section C (Compare Numbers to 99), lessons 14 to 23.

words: ten more; ten less; mentally
notes: Given a two-digit number, find 10 more or 10 less mentally without counting by ones, and explain: one more or one fewer ten (Progressions, PDF 63 (printed 57)). Base-ten blocks and drawings first, then without them. Limit: two-digit numbers. Cluster 1.NBT.C, major. IM Grade 1 unit 4 lessons 1 to 18, unit 6.

words: add; tens and tens; ones and ones; sum
notes: Begins 1.NBT.C.4 (owned by m1-add-within-100): add within 100 where no new ten is made, a two-digit and a one-digit number (43 + 5) and a two-digit number and a multiple of 10 (43 + 20), with blocks or drawings, and relate the strategy to a written equation. Tens are added to tens and ones to ones. Cluster 1.NBT.C, major. IM Grade 1 unit 5 section A (Add Without Making a Ten).

words: make a new ten; compose; add; explain
notes: Owns 1.NBT.C.4: add within 100, including a two-digit and a one-digit number and a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, when a new ten must be composed (46 + 7, then two-digit pairs such as 46 + 37) with blocks, drawings, properties and the relation to subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain it. Combining like units and making a ten extend the K and grade 1 make-ten methods (Progressions, PDF 63 (printed 57)). No standard algorithm required (that is grade 4). Cluster 1.NBT.C, major. IM Grade 1 unit 5 sections B and C.

words: subtract; tens; difference
notes: Subtract multiples of 10 from multiples of 10 in the range 10 to 90 with positive or zero differences (70 - 40 is 7 tens minus 4 tens; 80 - 70 as 70 + ? = 80), with blocks or drawings, related to a written method and explained. Limit: only multiples of 10; other two-digit subtraction is deferred to grade 2 so that subtracting with and without decomposing come close together and students avoid "subtract the smaller digit from the larger" (Progressions, PDF 63 (printed 57)). Cluster 1.NBT.C, major. IM Grade 1 unit 4 lessons 3 to 18, unit 5 lesson 14.

words: data; category; survey; tally; total; how many more
cross_subject: science:1-ESS1-2 (organise and compare observations in up to three groups)
notes: Organize, show and interpret data with up to three categories (tally marks, drawings, sorted objects; no set format is required), and ask and answer questions about the total, each category, and how many more or fewer in one than another, which practises 1.OA problem types (Progressions, PDF 82 (printed 76)). Picture graphs may appear but are not expected until grade 2. Limit: three categories. Teacher note: survey questions about favourites and objects, not about family income, bodies or home life. Cluster 1.MD.C, supporting. IM Grade 1 unit 1 sections B and C.

words: longer; longest; shorter; shortest; order; compare
notes: Order three objects by length and compare two lengths indirectly with a third object (a string as long as a forearm), with transitive reasoning: if A is longer than B and B than C, A is longer than C (Progressions, PDF 98 (printed 92)). Direct comparison with aligned endpoints is still checked. Limit: three objects in the ordering task. Cluster 1.MD.A, major. IM Grade 1 unit 6 section A (From Direct to Indirect Comparisons).

words: length unit; measure; end to end; no gaps; no overlaps
notes: Express a length as a whole number of same-size length units laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps. Limit (the standard's own): objects spanned by a whole number of units. Use same-size manipulative units (cubes, inch tiles) rather than many mixed nonstandard units, which can slow the idea down; a row of more units is not longer if the units are smaller (Progressions, PDF 98 to 99 (printed 92 to 93)). Measurements up to 120 units link to 1.NBT.A.1. Cluster 1.MD.A, major. IM Grade 1 unit 6 section B (Measure by Iterating up to 120 Length Units).

words: o'clock; half past; hour hand; minute hand; clock
notes: Tell and write time in hours and half hours on analog and digital clocks. On the analog clock the hour hand sits halfway between numbers at half past; misreading it is the typical error. Halves link to 1.G.A.3 (half past as half of the circle). Limit: hours and half hours only. The Progressions document has no section on telling time. Cluster 1.MD.B, additional. IM Grade 1 unit 7 section C (Tell Time in Hours and Half Hours).

words: attribute; side; corner; closed; open; triangle; square; rectangle
notes: Tell defining attributes (a triangle is closed with three straight sides) from non-defining ones (colour, orientation, overall size), and build and draw shapes that have given defining attributes (Progressions, PDF 125 (printed 119)). Sort shapes and explain why a shape belongs. Both flat and solid shapes are sorted. Cluster 1.G.A, additional. IM Grade 1 unit 7 section A, lessons 4 to 12.

words: compose; trapezoid; half-circle; quarter-circle; cube; prism; cone; cylinder
notes: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones and cylinders) into a composite shape, then use the composite as a new unit to make more shapes (a unit of units) (Progressions, PDF 121 (printed 115)). The shape list is the standard's own limit. Cluster 1.G.A, additional. IM Grade 1 unit 7 section A, lessons 2 to 17.

words: equal shares; halves; fourths; quarters; half of; fourth of
notes: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe them as halves, fourths and quarters (half of, a fourth of, a quarter of), describe the whole as two halves or four fourths, and see that more equal shares means smaller shares. Limit: circles and rectangles, 2 and 4 shares; no fraction notation (fractions as numbers are grade 3). Cluster 1.G.A, additional. IM Grade 1 unit 7 section B (Halves and Quarters).

words: just know; mental strategy; make a ten; doubles
notes: Fluently add and subtract within 20 with mental strategies (make a ten, doubles and near doubles, related facts), and by the end of grade 2 know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. Fluency has grown from within 5 (K) to within 10 (grade 1) to within 20 (grade 2); memory is the outcome of years of practice and reasoning, and students may fall back on strategies (Progressions, PDF 33 to 34 (printed 27 to 28)). Spaced, mixed, short practice all year; no timer shown to students. Cluster 2.OA.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 1 section A, unit 8, unit 9 section A, and warm-ups all year.

words: compare; tape diagram; unknown; equation
notes: One-step problems of all subtypes within 100, including the start-unknown and opposite-language Compare problems that grade 1 met without a proficiency target (Progressions, PDF 29 (printed 23)). Tape diagrams to compare (IM Grade 2 unit 1 section C, Diagrams to Compare) and equations with a symbol for the unknown; seven related equations for each fact (Progressions, PDF 33 (printed 27)). Contributes to 2.OA.A.1, owned by m2-two-step-problems. Cluster 2.OA.A, major. IM Grade 2 unit 1 section C and unit 2 section C.

words: two-step; first; then; tape diagram
cross_subject: ela:RI.2.1 (ask and answer who, what, how many questions to understand a text)
notes: Owns 2.OA.A.1: one- and two-step problems within 100 with unknowns in all positions. Two-step problems avoid the hardest subtypes and mostly use single-digit addends; those with a comparison may be shown with a drawing for one step and an equation for the other (Progressions, PDF 33 (printed 27)). Students also write problems for others. Tape diagrams and equations. Limit: within 100, addition and subtraction only. Cluster 2.OA.A, major. IM Grade 2 unit 2 section C, unit 3 (length contexts), unit 9 section C (Create and Solve Story Problems).

words: odd; even; pair; equal addends
notes: Decide whether a group of up to 20 objects is odd or even by pairing or counting by 2s, and write an even number as a sum of two equal addends (12 = 6 + 6). Ties doubles to odd and even (Progressions, PDF 40 (printed 34)). Limit: up to 20 objects. Cluster 2.OA.C, supporting: it practises addition and sets up grade 3 multiplication. IM Grade 2 unit 8 section A (Odd and Even).

words: array; row; column; equal addends; total
notes: Use addition to find the total in a rectangular array of up to 5 rows and 5 columns and write the total as a sum of equal addends (3 rows of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12). Introduces the array, carried into grade 3 multiplication; no multiplication sign yet (Progressions, PDF 40 (printed 34)). Limit: 5 by 5. Cluster 2.OA.C, supporting. IM Grade 2 unit 8 section B (Rectangular Arrays).

words: hundred; ten tens; bundle
notes: Ten tens can be thought of as one unit called a hundred, and 100, 200, ... 900 are one to nine hundreds and 0 tens 0 ones. Repeated bundling by 10 is the structure of the whole system (Progressions, PDF 64 (printed 58)). Base-ten blocks (flats) and quick drawings of a hundred as a square. Cluster 2.NBT.A, major. IM Grade 2 unit 5 section A, lessons 1 to 7.

words: hundreds; tens; ones; expanded form; three-digit number
notes: The three digits of a three-digit number are hundreds, tens and ones (706 is 7 hundreds 0 tens 6 ones; 0 holds the tens place), and numbers to 1000 are read and written as numerals, number names and expanded form (456 = 400 + 50 + 6). Students may still think of 500 as "the number after 499" and not as 5 hundreds (Progressions, PDF 64 (printed 58)). Blocks, drawings and layered place-value cards. Limit: to 1000. Cluster 2.NBT.A, major. IM Grade 2 unit 5 section A.

words: skip-count; by fives; by tens; by hundreds
notes: Count within 1000, especially across tens and hundreds (398, 399, 400), and skip-count by 5s, 10s and 100s from various starts, which shows the tens and hundreds in the sequence and prepares multiplication (Progressions, PDF 64 (printed 58)). Uses the number line from m2-number-line (IM places skip counts on it). Limit: within 1000. Cluster 2.NBT.A, major. IM Grade 2 units 1 to 7 as routines; unit 5 section A.

words: compare; greater than; less than; order
notes: Compare two three-digit numbers by their hundreds, tens and ones (845 > 799 because 8 hundreds is more than 7 hundreds and any tens and ones) and record with >, = and <; order numbers and place them on a number line (Progressions, PDF 64 (printed 58)). Limit: three-digit numbers. Cluster 2.NBT.A, major. IM Grade 2 unit 5 section B (Compare and Order Numbers within 1,000).

words: decompose a ten; compose a ten; add; subtract; strategy
notes: Begins 2.NBT.B.5 (owned by m2-fluency-within-100): add and subtract within 100 with blocks, drawings and equations, including subtraction that decomposes a ten (63 - 28), which grade 1 deferred so that subtracting with and without decomposing are taught close together (Progressions, PDF 63 and 66 (printed 57 and 60)). Strategies: place value, properties, adding on to subtract. Do not linger: long practice of subtraction within 100 by counting on or down slows later work (Progressions, PDF 66 (printed 60)). Cluster 2.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 2 sections A and B (Decompose to Subtract).

words: fluently; mentally; strategy
notes: Owns 2.NBT.B.5: fluently add and subtract within 100 with strategies based on place value, properties and the relation of addition and subtraction; written methods that record new units are allowed, blocks are not part of fluency. The standard algorithm is not expected until grade 4 (Progressions, PDF 65 (printed 59)). Spaced practice through units 3, 4, 6, 7 and 9. No timer shown. Cluster 2.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 2, unit 4, unit 9 section A.

words: add; group; tens; ones
notes: Add up to four two-digit numbers using place value and properties (reorder and group to make tens: 25 + 37 + 15 + 3). Limit: up to four addends, each two-digit; totals may pass 100. Cluster 2.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 2 lessons 7 to 16, unit 6 lessons 14 to 20 (money and length sums).

words: ten more; ten less; one hundred more; one hundred less
notes: Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from a number from 100 to 900, explaining which digit changes and why, including across a hundred (395 + 10). Limit: given numbers 100 to 900. Cluster 2.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 5 lessons 10 to 12 and unit 7.

words: compose; hundreds; tens; ones; add
notes: Begins 2.NBT.B.7 (owned by m2-subtract-within-1000): add within 1000 with blocks, drawings and place-value strategies, first without composing, then composing tens, hundreds or both (278 + 147), and relate each step to a written method; methods that record new units below the line help the move toward a shorter written method, which all students need by grade 4 (Progressions, PDF 65 to 66 (printed 59 to 60)). Cluster 2.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 7 sections A and B.

words: decompose; hundreds; tens; ones; subtract
notes: Owns 2.NBT.B.7: subtract within 1000 with blocks, drawings and place-value strategies, decomposing a hundred or a ten when needed (425 - 278), related to a written method; also as an unknown addend (278 + ? = 425). Common error: forgetting to decompose after subtracting in the ones (Progressions, PDF 66 (printed 60)). Limit: within 1000. Cluster 2.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 7 section C.

words: explain; why it works; same; different
cross_subject: ela:SL.2.1 (build on others' talk when comparing strategies)
notes: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work using place value and properties, with drawings or objects, and compare two methods for the same problem (MP.3, MP.1) (Progressions, PDF 59 to 60 and 65 (printed 53 to 54 and 59)). Spread through units 2 and 7; one written or spoken explanation per section is checked. Cluster 2.NBT.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 2 lessons 2 to 10, unit 7 lessons 4 to 18.

words: ruler; centimeter; meter; inch; foot; yard; estimate
cross_subject: science:2-LS2-1 (measure plant height with a ruler)
notes: Measure lengths with the right tool (ruler, yardstick, meter stick, measuring tape) in centimeters, meters, inches and feet, starting from 0 and counting length units, not marks; first rulers can be made by students from iterated units (Progressions, PDF 103 (printed 97)). Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters with benchmarks (Progressions, PDF 105 (printed 99)). Measurements to the nearest whole unit. Cluster 2.MD.A, major. IM Grade 2 unit 3 sections A and B.

words: unit; larger unit; fewer units
notes: Measure one object twice with units of different lengths (inches and centimeters) and explain the inverse relation: the larger the unit, the fewer units it takes (Progressions, PDF 103 (printed 97)). Limit: whole units. Cluster 2.MD.A, major. IM Grade 2 unit 3 lessons 1 to 9.

words: how much longer; difference; compare
notes: Measure two objects and find how much longer one is than the other in a standard unit, by subtracting or counting on along the ruler (Progressions, PDF 104 (printed 98)). Links Compare problems to length. Limit: whole standard units. Cluster 2.MD.A, major. IM Grade 2 unit 3 lessons 2 to 18.

words: total length; how much longer; missing length
notes: Solve word problems about lengths in the same unit with addition and subtraction within 100, using drawings of rulers, tape diagrams and equations with a symbol for the unknown; adding lengths is part of the move from whole-number to fraction addition (Progressions, PDF 34 and 104 (printed 28 and 98)). Limit: within 100, same units. Cluster 2.MD.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 3 lessons 6 to 18 and unit 4 lessons 9 to 13.

words: number line; tick mark; length unit; jump
notes: Introduces the number-line diagram: whole numbers as lengths from 0 with equally spaced points 0, 1, 2, ..., and sums and differences within 100 as jumps. Number lines are held back until grade 2, after rulers, because young children count marks or the 0 instead of length units and make off-by-one errors (Progressions, PDF 32 (printed 26)); a number line is like a ruler, with consecutive whole numbers one unit apart (PDF 104 (printed 98)). Limit: within 100 for sums and differences. Cluster 2.MD.B, major. IM Grade 2 unit 4 (Addition and Subtraction on the Number Line).

words: a.m.; p.m.; minutes; quarter past; quarter to
notes: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.; skip-counting by 5s (2.NBT.A.2) reads the minute hand, and quarter past and half past link to 2.G.A.3. Limit: nearest five minutes; elapsed time is grade 3. The Progressions document has no section on time. Cluster 2.MD.C, supporting. IM Grade 2 unit 6 section C (Time on the Clock).

words: dollar; cents; quarter; dime; nickel; penny
notes: Solve word problems with dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies, using the $ and cent symbols correctly (2 dimes 3 pennies is 23 cents). Coin values practise skip-counting and place value; no decimal notation for money (that is grade 4). Teacher note: use made-up prices and play money; avoid problems that make a child's family spending the topic. Limit: whole dollars or whole cents in a problem. Cluster 2.MD.C, supporting. IM Grade 2 unit 6 section D (The Value of Money).

words: line plot; data; measurement; scale
cross_subject: science:2-LS2-1 (measure several plants and show the heights)
notes: Make measurement data by measuring several objects to the nearest whole unit, or one object several times, and show it on a line plot with a whole-number scale. A line-plot scale is a ruler (Progressions, PDF 105 (printed 99)). Introduces the dot-plot model name (a line plot is a dot plot). Limit: whole units. Cluster 2.MD.D, supporting. IM Grade 2 unit 3 section C (Line Plots).

words: picture graph; bar graph; category; scale; key
cross_subject: science:2-LS4-1 (picture graph of how many kinds were found in each place)
notes: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph with a single-unit scale for data in up to four categories, and solve put-together, take-apart and compare problems from a bar graph (Progressions, PDF 80 and 34 (printed 74 and 28)). Introduces the bar-graph model name (picture graphs and bar graphs); scaled graphs are grade 3. Limit: up to four categories, scale of one. Cluster 2.MD.D, supporting. IM Grade 2 unit 1 section B (Ways to Represent Data).

words: angle; face; triangle; quadrilateral; pentagon; hexagon; cube
notes: Recognize and draw shapes with given attributes (a number of angles, a number of equal faces), and identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons and cubes (Progressions, PDF 127 (printed 121)). Angles are counted, not measured (angle measure is grade 4). Cluster 2.G.A, additional. IM Grade 2 unit 6 section A (Attributes of Shapes).

words: row; column; same-size squares; partition
notes: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count the squares. Seeing a row as one unit and as several squares is spatial structuring, which comes before area (grade 3) and harder than often assumed (Progressions, PDF 105 and 128 (printed 99 and 122)). Grade 1 composing of units of units is the prior work. No area units or multiplication yet. Cluster 2.G.A, additional. IM Grade 2 unit 8 lessons 11 to 12.

words: halves; thirds; fourths; equal shares; whole
notes: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three or four equal shares, describe them (halves, thirds, half of, a third of) and the whole (two halves, three thirds, four fourths), and recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape (Progressions, PDF 127 (printed 121)). Limit: 2, 3 or 4 shares; no fraction notation (grade 3 unit fractions build on this). Cluster 2.G.A, additional. IM Grade 2 unit 6 section B (Halves, Thirds, and Fourths).
